description_full: Allwyn AG engages in the operation of lotteries, casinos, and sports and other odds betting in Austria, Czech Republic, Greece, Cyprus, Italy, the United Kingdom, Belgium, Germany, and the United States. It also engages in operating video lottery terminals, online lottery games, online instant win games, online casino, and slot gaming. In addition, the company offers mobile telecommunication services, including voice, message, and data to retail customers, as well as phone top-up services. Further, it sells food and beverages. The company was founded in 1958 and is based in Lucerne, Switzerland.

financial_summary: OPAP S.A. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $18.0B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 53% against a 9% cost of capital — a 44-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 73% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $746M in free cash flow — roughly 41 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.48× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -10.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 24× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 75% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 5.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
